quizzes.title: Identity and Demand Bases
quizzes.passage:
The Gorkhaland issue concerns a demand for a separate political or administrative arrangement for the Gorkha population of the Darjeeling Hills in West Bengal. Supporters of the movement say that the people of the hills have their own language, culture and social character, and that these set them apart from the wider population of the state. Much of the case therefore rests on the idea of a distinct identity.

Beyond identity, the movement has raised questions of dignity and representation. Its supporters believe the community needs a stronger political voice and that its concerns have not carried enough weight in decisions about the region. Such concerns have been present for a long time, and they continue to shape how the debate is framed.

Economic concerns form a second strand of the argument. The hills are said to have faced job shortages and long periods of neglect in development planning. Demands for greater control over decisions and public money are closely tied to these grievances. Supporters also point out that the region contributes to the state's economy through its natural and commercial activities.

The movement has a long history. Its early political demands can be traced to the start of the twentieth century, and the agitation that followed gave the movement great momentum. Today the discussion centres on how governance, finance and development should be organised for the hill region within the existing constitutional system.

questions.q: The Darjeeling Hills population is described as having a distinct linguistic, cultural and social identity compared with which group?
questions.explanation: The booklet contrasts the hills' distinct identity with the Bengali-majority plains.

questions.q: Besides political autonomy, the demand for Gorkhaland also raises concerns about insufficient which kind of autonomy?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists insufficient political and fiscal autonomy among the region's economic and developmental concerns.

questions.q: Concerns over identity insecurity and which other factor have contributed to demands for stronger political recognition and representation?
questions.explanation: The booklet names racial stereotyping alongside identity insecurity as a driver of demands for political recognition.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Gorkhaland demand is based only on identity considerations.
Reason (R): Economic concerns such as infrastructure and employment are also part of the case for greater recognition.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet lists economic and developmental concerns as a major basis of the demand, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Predominant language of the hill region   ->   A. Darjeeling Tea, Forestry and Tourism
II. Institution giving greater autonomy to the hill region   ->   B. Nepali
III. Sector cited as a regional contribution   ->   C. Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council
IV. Long-standing economic concern   ->   D. Inadequate infrastructure
questions.explanation: The region's predominant language is Nepali, the Hill Council gave greater autonomy, tea-forestry-tourism is a regional contribution, and infrastructure is a long-standing concern.

questions.q:
Statements:
I. The Darjeeling Hills population is described as having a distinct linguistic identity.
II. Proponents seek separation of the community from India.
III. Concerns over identity insecurity have contributed to demands for stronger political recognition and representation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II reverses its point that proponents seek recognition within India rather than separation.

questions.q:
Statements:
Statement 1: The region has a predominantly Nepali-speaking population.
Statement 2: Proponents seek separation of the community from India.
Statement 3: The region contributes through Darjeeling Tea, Forestry and Tourism.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are stated in the booklet, while statement 2 is not, so only two are correct.

questions.q: Which language is predominantly spoken in the Darjeeling Hills region? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the region has a predominantly Nepali-speaking population.

questions.q: Concerns over identity insecurity and which other factor have contributed to demands for stronger political recognition? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet links identity insecurity with racial stereotyping as contributors to political demands.

questions.q: Along with Forestry and Tourism, which product of the region is named as a contribution? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Darjeeling Tea, Forestry and Tourism as sectors through which the region contributes.

questions.q: Besides political autonomy, insufficient which kind of autonomy is listed as a concern? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists insufficient political and fiscal autonomy as a concern.

questions.q: Proponents seek recognition of the community as an integral part of which country? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says proponents want recognition as an integral part of India rather than separation from the country.

questions.q: The Darjeeling Hills identity is described as distinct from which plains population? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet compares the hills' identity with the Bengali-majority plains.

questions.q: The supporters' basis of demand built on language and culture is titled 'Ethno-' what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet headlines this basis of demand as Ethno-Linguistic Identity.

quizzes.title: Talks, Committee and Challenges
quizzes.passage:
Talks on the Gorkhaland question have entered a new phase. A meeting involving the state government and representatives of the Gorkha community was held recently, and the Union Government then set up a committee to take the matter forward. The committee has been asked to prepare an agreement and to lay out the steps needed for a lasting settlement.

The committee will look at the issue in light of the country's basic law. Its scope covers how the region should be governed, the financial support it receives and the development programmes that can be pursued. It will also work on a roadmap for several Gorkha communities to receive a special category of recognition.

Not everyone agrees on the path ahead. In parts of the state there is opposition to any division of territory, and those who hold this view are concerned about the unity of the state and the smooth working of its administration. The political landscape is also crowded, since the Gorkha side is represented by several organisations, which makes a shared stand hard to reach.

The region's location adds weight to the issue. Long unrest in the hills could affect more than local life, because the area lies in a sensitive position that matters for the wider country. The local economy depends heavily on plantations and visitors, and it faces difficulties that shift with the seasons and with longer trends. Any new arrangement would need a sound economic base to survive.

questions.q: Which ministry of the Union Government convened the recent Tripartite Meeting on the Gorkhaland issue?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Ministry of Home Affairs convened the Tripartite Meeting.

questions.q: Within which framework will the committee examine the Gorkhaland issue?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the committee will examine the issue within the Constitutional Framework.

questions.q: What critical function does the Siliguri Corridor serve for India?
options: Principal land link between mainland India and the Northeast
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Siliguri Corridor as the principal land link between mainland India and the Northeast.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Gorkha political landscape is dominated by a single organisation.
Reason (R): Multiple Gorkha organisations make it difficult to agree on a common position.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet describes a fragmented Gorkha landscape with multiple organisations, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Countries close to the Darjeeling region   ->   D. Structural and seasonal economic challenges
II. Group making a common position difficult   ->   B. Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh
III. Concern behind opposition to territorial division   ->   A. Gorkha Janmukti Morcha
IV. Economic sustainability challenge   ->   C. Administrative cohesion
questions.explanation: The region lies close to Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh, Gorkha Janmukti Morcha is among the fragmenting groups, administrative cohesion is a concern, and the economy faces structural and seasonal challenges.

questions.q:
Statements:
I. Opposition in parts of West Bengal to territorial division reflects concerns over territorial integrity.
II. Prolonged instability in the region has only local implications for tea production.
III. The regional economy depends on tea, tourism and related activities, which face structural and seasonal challenges.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are stated in the booklet, while statement II is contradicted by its point that instability has wider strategic and security implications.

questions.q:
Statements:
Statement 1: The Union Government constituted a committee to work out modalities for a Permanent Political Solution.
Statement 2: The Siliguri Corridor lies close to Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
Statement 3: The committee's work will be limited to the number of Lok Sabha seats in the state.
Statement 4: The committee will examine the issue within the Constitutional Framework.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are in the booklet, while statement 3 is not, so exactly three are correct.

questions.q: Besides Nepal and Bhutan, which country lies close to the Darjeeling region? (one word)

questions.q: Apart from tea, which activity supports the regional economy? (one word)

questions.q: Prolonged instability in the region can have wider strategic and which other implications? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that prolonged instability can have wider strategic and national security implications.

questions.q: The committee will work out a roadmap for granting which status to several Gorkha communities? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the committee will work out a roadmap for granting Scheduled Tribe status to Gorkha communities.
